title: OpenBox Developer-Runtime Normalized Event
description: Tool-agnostic, versioned ADAPTER-FACING event contract for developer-runtime coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor). Every provider adapter maps its native payload onto this shape (SPI emit()). The OpenBox client then RE-EXPRESSES it onto the base SDK's unified wire model — WorkflowStarted/WorkflowCompleted/SignalReceived/ActivityStarted+hook_trigger — on POST /api/v1/governance/evaluate (see MAPPING.md; ADR-0004). This is NOT a verbatim event_type pass-through: the SL-1 EXT-core accept-list is retired (E7-S2). Adding a provider never changes this contract or the wire model (PRD FR-4, architecture §1b). Verified against openbox-core internal/content/{governance,session}.go and the base contract openbox-sdk-python/openbox_core/contracts/events.py (spikes S6, S8/E7-S0).

x-changelog.1.4: Adds `content.thinking` (ADR-0019 P3) — the model's extended-thinking text for a turn, its `thinking` content blocks concatenated in file order across the turn's transcript window, landing in the wire payload's `activity_output.thinking` on a TurnCompleted. This is the bump that AMENDS ADR-0014's transcript allowlist: the projection that reads token counts out of the session transcript now binds one free-form CONTENT string, where before it bound only an identifier, a timestamp and a bool. The transcript is the only source — no hook payload carries thinking, and Claude Code's own OTel export redacts it unconditionally with every content flag enabled, so capturing it goes further than the provider itself will. It rides activity_output rather than the assistant span (ADR-0018) deliberately: that span feeds core's goal-alignment extractor, which reads it as the assistant's REPLY, and chain-of-thought there would score every later turn's drift against the model's reasoning instead of its answer. Content-gated (INV-2) — absent unless the org opted in — redacted at source before attachment and capped at 64KB before signing. Purely additive: every 1.3 event is a valid 1.4 event, and an org with content capture off sends byte-identical payloads.
x-changelog.1.3: Adds `content.tool_output` (ADR-0019 P1) — what a tool PRODUCED, carried on ToolResult and landing in the wire payload's `activity_output.output`, the field core stores as the row's `output` and runs Guardrails stage 1 over. A failed call carries its own free-text error there instead of a result body; `status` already says which it is. This is the change that RETIRES SL3-SEC-3 ("tool commands and file bodies never egress on observe events"): tool input now also rides `content.tool_input` on the observe ToolCall, not only on a gated call's evaluation event. Also adds `content.signal_detail` for the PermissionDenied / APIError free text, which reaches `metadata` and deliberately never `signal_args`. Both are content-gated (INV-2) — absent unless the org opted in — redacted at source before attachment and capped at 64KB before signing. `content.tool_input` itself is not new to the wire (ADR-0017 attached it to gated calls); it was simply never listed here, and is documented in this bump. Purely additive: every 1.2 event is a valid 1.3 event.
x-changelog.1.2: Adds `status` on tool results (ADR-0018 Decision 1) — the field openbox-core's per-tool success metric reads and no producer had ever written, which pinned Tool Health SUCCESS at 0%. Closed enum completed|failed, ToolResult only (payload.status also writes the row's workflow_status column, so it must not ride a lifecycle event), derived structurally and NOT content-gated. Also adds the failure/lifecycle event types SubagentStarted/PermissionDenied/APIError, which ride stock SignalReceived. Purely additive: every 1.1 event is a valid 1.2 event.
x-changelog.1.1: Adds the turn pair (TurnStarted/TurnCompleted → ActivityStarted/ActivityCompleted with activity_type llm_completion, ADR-0014) and the fields it needs: model, turn_index, agent_id. Widens $defs.tokens with cache_creation_input/cache_read and RE-DEFINES `input` as PURE input — the Claude Code SessionEnd rollup used to fold both cache counts into it. Additive except for that one semantic, which is why this is a version bump and not a silent edit.
x-changelog.1.0: Initial contract (ADR-0004 base wire unification; ADR-0013 retired the span layer without changing this shape).

schema_version.description: Version of THIS event contract carried on the wire. Bumped on a breaking change to the normalized shape.

event_id.description: Client-generated unique id for idempotent ingestion (INV-5). Retries/buffered flush reuse the same id so tokens/cost/lineage are never double-counted.

event_type.description: Developer-runtime LIFECYCLE type (adapter-facing). NOTE: CommitCreated is RESERVED — the schema branch and wire mapping exist but no adapter produces it; commit lineage flows through the git trailer and notes into the Deploy event's metadata instead. The client re-maps each onto a base-SDK wire type: SessionStarted->WorkflowStarted, SessionEnded->WorkflowCompleted, PromptSubmitted/CommitCreated/Deploy->SignalReceived(signal_name), ToolCall/ToolResult->ActivityStarted/ActivityCompleted (paired by a shared activity_id; ADR-0013 retired the span layer), TurnStarted/TurnCompleted->ActivityStarted/ActivityCompleted with activity_type llm_completion (paired by activity_id <session>:turn:<index>; ADR-0014). NOT a verbatim core event_type; the EXT-core accept-list is retired (E7-S2). See MAPPING.md §2.

openbox_session_id.description: Opaque logical session id. The client synthesizes core's jointly-unique NOT-NULL (workflow_id, run_id) from it: run_id = openbox_session_id, workflow_id = a stable per-workspace/developer identity (e.g. developer_did or repo). Both required (S6 §4).

developer_did.description: The developer/session agent DID. Shares the runtime-agent DID namespace (INV-7). Reuses agent/create identity (agent_type=developer, S6 §1).

timestamp.description: Event time, RFC3339. Maps verbatim to core payload's string `timestamp`.

started_at.description: Optional start time for spanning events (ToolCall/session). RFC3339.

ended_at.description: Optional end time for spanning events (ToolResult/session). RFC3339.

model.description: Provider model id that spent this event's tokens ('claude-opus-4-8', 'gpt-5-codex'). Identifier-class metadata, NOT content (INV-2) — it is the one free-form string the transcript/rollout usage projections egress, and it is bounded at the adapter boundary. Load-bearing: the backend aggregates token rollups under model-keyed composite metric keys, so a turn with no model is invisible to the dashboards it feeds. Absent when the projection found none — never back-filled from the session's model, which would attribute tokens to a model that may not have spent them.

turn_index.description: Zero-based index of the model turn this event belongs to, within its session (or within its subagent). Both halves of a turn pair carry the same value; the client derives activity_id = <session>[:agent:<agent_id>]:turn:<index> from it, which is what pairs them onto one row. Set on TurnStarted/TurnCompleted only.

agent_id.description: Subagent this event occurred inside. On turn events it partitions the activity_id so a subagent's turns never collide with the main thread's. Empty/absent on the main thread. Structural identifier (INV-2).

status.description: Outcome of a tool call (v1.2, ADR-0018 Decision 1). Set on ToolResult ONLY — the client drops it on every other event type, because core copies payload.status into the row's workflow_status column for ANY event type (activities/governance/storage_event.go:417) and a lifecycle event's workflow_status means something else. This scope cannot be expressed in the subset of JSON Schema the conformance validator implements, so it is enforced by client.statusFor and asserted on the outbound bytes by conformance case C20. Structural, NOT content (INV-2): derived from which provider hook fired, or from a bound bool/int — never parsed from tool output — so it is not content-gated and ships identically with content_capture off. Core reads the literal 'completed' and nothing else (observability/errors.go:333), which is why the enum is closed rather than free-form.

metadata.description: Additive per-type key/values. Lands verbatim in core payload's `metadata` (json.RawMessage). Never carries credentials/secrets (INV-1) or raw content (INV-2 — content lives only under `content`).

deploy_did.description: DID minted for the deploy = git hash + timestamp (FR-6).

oneOf.title: TurnStarted
oneOf.description: Opens one model turn. turn_index is required because the client derives the pair's activity_id from it; without it the pair cannot correlate. Carries no usage — the numbers are known only at the close.

oneOf.title: TurnCompleted
oneOf.description: Closes one model turn and carries what it spent: tokens (all four counts the provider reports) and the model that spent them. Both are optional — a turn the projection could not measure is still a real turn, and zero-filling would claim it spent nothing.

oneOf.title: SubagentStarted
oneOf.description: A subagent spawned (v1.2, ADR-0018). Rides SignalReceived(subagent_started). Metadata-only: agent_id + agent_type. Carries NO signal_args — core's alignment engine treats any SignalReceived with non-empty signal_args as a NEW USER GOAL and overwrites the session's goal with them (openbox-core internal/services/age.go:112-137), so structural detail rides metadata for all three of these signals.

oneOf.title: PermissionDenied
oneOf.description: A policy or classifier refused a tool call (v1.2, ADR-0018). Rides SignalReceived(permission_denied). Records THAT a decision happened and which tool it was about — never the content and never the reason (the provider's `reason` is free text and is not bound; ADR-0019 owns it). Note the provider limit: Claude Code 2.1.229 fires its PermissionDenied hook only after an auto-mode classifier denial, so a static deny rule denies WITHOUT producing this event — absence is not evidence that nothing was denied.

oneOf.title: APIError
oneOf.description: A model turn ended in a provider-side error instead of an answer (v1.2, ADR-0018). Rides SignalReceived(api_error). metadata.error_type is the provider's own closed enum (rate_limit, overloaded, authentication_failed, oauth_org_not_allowed, billing_error, invalid_request, model_not_found, server_error, max_output_tokens, unknown), allowlisted at the adapter; anything else is dropped rather than egressed. Free-text error detail is NOT carried.

tool.description: The developer tool/action that produced the event. `kind` is the provider-agnostic tool class; `mcp_server` is required when kind=mcp (enforced by the conformance harness).

name.description: Native tool name, e.g. 'Bash', 'Edit', 'mcp__github__create_issue'. Metadata only (INV-2).

kind.description: Provider-agnostic tool class. shell=command execution; file=file read/write/open/delete; mcp=MCP tool call.

tokens.description: Token usage for the turn or the session rollup (metadata only). Absent when unknown; each count absent rather than zero when the provider does not report it. Since v1.1 `input` is PURE input and the two cache counts have their own fields — v1.0's Claude Code rollup folded both into `input`, which made cache efficiency unmeasurable and a cache-heavy session look like it had spent its whole context on fresh input.

input.description: Prompt tokens that were neither served from nor written to the prompt cache.

cache_creation_input.description: Input tokens WRITTEN to the prompt cache (Anthropic cache_creation_input_tokens; Codex cache_write_input_tokens).

cache_read.description: Input tokens SERVED from the prompt cache (Anthropic cache_read_input_tokens; Codex cached_input_tokens).

total.description: Whole throughput: input + output + both cache counts.

cost.description: Monetary cost for the turn/tool (metadata only). Absent when unknown.

span.description: One semantic span for a tool call/result. Mirrors the subset of openbox-core SpanData an adapter SETS; core COMPUTES `semantic_type` server-side from these source fields (S6 §2) — the value here is the intended target and a hint. Carried in the core payload's `spans[]`.

semantic_type.description: Target openbox-core span semantic type. Subset relevant to developer tools; all values exist in core session.go (S6 §2, verified).

stage.description: Maps to core SpanData.stage. ToolCall emits 'started'; ToolResult emits 'completed'.

invocation_id.description: THIS attempt at the operation (the provider's tool_use_id). Pairs a call's started and completed spans onto one span_id and keys the duration stash. LOCAL: normalized-event and spool only — never emitted as a field on the core wire payload, where it survives solely as an input to the opaque span_id hash.

operation_id.description: WHAT the call does, identical across a RETRY of the same operation, so an approval can be consumed by the retry: activity_id derives from it, activity_id is the approval key, and core scopes both bypass grants by activity_id. Per class — shell: a hash of the command; MCP: a hash of the argument shape; otherwise the invocation (classes with no structural discriminator are never gated). Structural or hashed, never content (INV-2). LOCAL, like invocation_id: an input to the opaque activity_id hash, never a wire field.

request_body.description: Tool input content. GATED (INV-2): present only when content-capture is enabled for the org; Guardrail-redacted at source, and capped to 65536 chars before egress (capBody, G_SEC SEC-1). Maps to core SpanData.request_body.

response_body.description: Tool output content. GATED (INV-2); capped to 65536 chars before egress (capBody, G_SEC SEC-1). Maps to core SpanData.response_body.

content.description: The ONLY location for raw prompt/output/file content. GATED (INV-2/OD4): absent by default; present only when an org opts in, and then Guardrail-redacted at source before egress. The conformance harness rejects any event carrying this when content-capture is disabled.

tool_input.description: What a tool was asked to do — the shell command, the MCP arguments, the file body. Rides the gated call's evaluation event (ADR-0017) and, since v1.3, the observe-path ToolCall as well. Lands in the wire payload's activity_input under a per-class key (command|arguments|content), because a reviewer reading `command: <a file body>` would be misled about what was executed.

signal_detail.description: A lifecycle signal's free text (v1.3, ADR-0019 P1): why a classifier refused a call (PermissionDenied), what the provider said when a turn failed (APIError). Lands in the wire payload's metadata under a per-type key — denial_reason / error_details — beside that signal's structural fields. It must NEVER land in signal_args: core's alignment engine reads any SignalReceived with non-empty signal_args as a NEW USER GOAL and overwrites the session's goal with it (internal/services/age.go:112-137), so a denial reason routed there would replace the developer's prompt as the thing every later turn is scored against. Conformance case C38 asserts both halves.

thinking.description: The model's extended-thinking text for a turn (v1.4, ADR-0019 P3): its `thinking` content blocks, concatenated in file order across the turn's transcript window, bounded so a single window cannot hold unbounded text. Lands in the wire payload's `activity_output.thinking` on TurnCompleted, where core runs Guardrails stage 1 and OPA over it — reasoning a policy can see is reasoning a policy can judge. Deliberately NOT on the assistant span (ADR-0018): that span exists to feed core's goal-alignment extractor, which reads it as the assistant's REPLY, so chain-of-thought there would score every later turn's drift against the model's reasoning instead of its answer, and would fail silently. This field is the one that AMENDS ADR-0014's transcript allowlist — the first free-form content string that projection binds — so its gate, its redaction and its cap are each asserted on outbound bytes rather than trusted.

tool_output.description: What a tool PRODUCED — the result body of a completed call, or the tool's own free-text error when it failed (v1.3, ADR-0019 P1). Lands in the wire payload's activity_output.output. Deliberately NOT `output`, which carries the assistant's turn text (ADR-0018): overloading one field across both would put turn text on tool events and tool output into core's goal-alignment extractor the moment either mapping slipped.

verdict.description: Canonical governance verdict for PARSING /evaluate responses. Priority: HALT > BLOCK > REQUIRE_APPROVAL > CONSTRAIN > ALLOW. NOTE: openbox-core serializes the response `verdict` field as the LOWERCASE wire strings in x-wire-mapping (verified S6, governance.go MarshalJSON), and also emits a legacy `action` field (x-legacy-action). Phase-1 observe treats every verdict as allow (D7/INV-3). CONSTRAIN is core's sandbox-enforcement tier (Verdict=1), beyond the story's 4-value set — see G3_REVIEW finding.
